office_does: A Skamania County PUD commissioner is one of three board members who set rates, budgets, borrowing and projects for the county's public electric utility and the Carson and Underwood water systems; nominated from District 3, elected by the whole county, six-year term.
race_blurb: Board president Liz Green, commissioner for 12 years, faces Addison Dillon of Carson, a first-time candidate. Green defends a debt-financed rebuild of the 90-year-old system; Dillon says the $60 monthly residential basic charge is the state's highest and wants major spending explained before rate increases, a freeze on commissioner raises and a plain-language 'Ratepayer Report Card'. No rubric axis applies to PUD races.

candidates.summary: PUD commissioner for District 3 for 12 years and the board's president; lives in Cook.
highlights: Says the PUD is rebuilding substations and water treatment plants and replacing reservoirs [S2]
Financed with bonds, grants and loans and a rate structure spread over decades [S2]
Cites rising regulatory costs and power-shortage risk [S1]

candidates.summary: Skamania County native from Carson with a career in the service industry; first run for office.
highlights: Says the residential basic charge rose from $8.45 in 2009 to $60, the highest in Washington [S2][S6]
Would require a public cost-and-benefit explanation before major projects or new debt [S2]
Would oppose commissioner pay raises until rates stabilize [S2]
Proposes a monthly 'Ratepayer Report Card' on every bill [S3]
Raised $2,560, including $500 from the county Democrats [S7][S8]
